| Modeling Period | Advantage | Limitation |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Jan 2010 – June 2025 | Long historical record | Multiple structural changes |
| Jan 2024 – June 2025 | More recent enrollment environment | May capture unwinding and expansion effects |
| July 2024 – June 2025 | Most recent 12-month trend | Shorter modeling period |

Start with January 2024 and compare the results against the other periods as a sensitivity analysis.

```{r, include=FALSE}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE,message = FALSE,echo=FALSE)

# Set up workspace-----------------------

# Connect to postgres
library(dplyr)
library(RPostgres)
library(tidyr)
library(tidycensus)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(rpostgis)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# Connect to postgres

source("W:\\RDA Team\\R\\credentials_source.R")

con <- connect_to_db("eqb_hr1_tracker")
con_shared<-connect_to_db("rda_shared_data")
drv <- dbDriver("PostgreSQL")

# Read in tables from postgres:

medical_race_raw<-dbGetQuery(con_shared, "SELECT * FROM health.cchs_medical_eligibles_race_age_county_2010_26")

# what is the range of data we have: Jan 2010 - October 2026. We know October 2025 is misisng.

medical_race_raw%>%
  select(month_of_eligibility)%>%
  View()

# Get total enrollment not by race:

medical_enrollment<-medical_race_raw%>%
  group_by(month_of_eligibility, county)%>%
  summarise(total=sum(total_eligibles))%>%
  ungroup()

# Set baseline date variables

baseline_date <- as.Date("2025-06-01") # same baseline used in all our analysis tables
model_start <- as.Date("2024-01-01") # start date 
end_date <- as.Date("2026-10-01") # end date: most recent month/year of data

# Prep df for regressions-------------------------

enrollment_df <- medical_enrollment %>%
  mutate(month = ym(month_of_eligibility)) %>% # convert column to ym date format
  select(county, month, enrollment = total) %>% # select columns of interest
  group_by(county) %>%
  complete(month = seq.Date(as.Date("2010-01-01"),end_date, by = "month")) %>% # creates a row for every month for every county, including October 2025, with NA for missing enrollment values. This way the month/years that have NA values are not completely missing
  arrange(month) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    time = (year(month) - 2010) * 12 + month(month) - 1) # number of months that have elapsed since January 2010, which is earliest month/year in our data. We want the calendar dates to be a continuous numeric variable that can be used in a regression model to estimate how Medi-Cal enrollment changes over time.

```

# Method 1: Baseline-anchored linear trend projection

I am using using a regression to estimate the historical rate of change in enrollment over time. I am taking the slope of the regression line and anchoring it to the actual June 2025 enrollment count. From there I am projecting what enrollment should be after June 2025 using the formula?: baseline enrollment number +  (historical rate of enrollment change) x (months elapsed since baseline time)

For this we define the baseline time as: June 2025 

```{r}

# PROJECTION METHOD 1: Historical rate of change----------------------------------

df <- enrollment_df %>%
  group_by(county) %>% # model for each county separately
  group_modify(~ {

    # Select the window of historical enrollment data to base trends off of, or the 'before HR 1' window of time
    pre_data <- .x %>%
      filter(
        month >= model_start,
        month <= baseline_date,
        !is.na(enrollment) # excluse NA enrollment data
      )

    # Get actual enrollment at baseline:  number of Medi-Cal enrollees in June 2025 for each county
    
    baseline <- .x %>%
      filter(month == baseline_date) %>%
      pull(enrollment)

    # Skip counties with insufficient data
    if (nrow(pre_data) < 12 || # Does the county have fewer than 12 months of valid enrollment values
        length(baseline) != 1 || # Is there not exactly one enrollment observation for June 2025 (baseline)?
        anyNA(baseline)) { # 	Is the June 2025 (baseline) enrollment count missing?

      return(.x %>%
        mutate(
          projected_enrollment = NA_real_,
          enrollment_gap = NA_real_,
          enrollment_gap_pct = NA_real_
        ))
    }

    # Now create simple linear regression to identify the straight line that best describes the relationship between time and Medi-Cal enrollment during the historical period.
    
    pre_model <- lm(
      enrollment ~ time,
      data = pre_data
    )

    # Extract monthly enrollment trend or the slope of the linear regression line: This will tell us how many enrollees the county historically gained or lost per month, on average, according to the fitted linear trend.
  
      monthly_trend <- unname(coef(pre_model)["time"])

    # Get baseline time: How many months passed between Jan 2010 and the baseline time (June 2025) 
    baseline_time <- .x %>%
      filter(month == baseline_date) %>%
      pull(time)

    # Project enrollment starting at June 2025:
    # the formula is essentially: baseline enrollment +  monthly trend (the slope of the linear regression) * months since baseline) to essentially say, using the rate generated from our linear model, and we apply that rate to subsequent time after our baseline, what would projected enrollment be? 
    
    .x %>%
      mutate(
        projected_enrollment = if_else(
          month >= baseline_date,
          baseline + monthly_trend * (time - baseline_time),
          NA_real_
        ),

  # Then calculate gaps between projected enrollment and the real enrollment data
        enrollment_gap =
          enrollment - projected_enrollment,
# enrollment gap percentage is better because takes into account diff population sizes for the counties
        enrollment_gap_pct =
          100 * enrollment_gap / projected_enrollment
      )

  }) %>%
  ungroup()


```

Below is the projection visualized just for Los Angeles County. 

```{r}

# METHOD 1: Visualize for LA county only: 

df %>%
  filter(
    county == "Los Angeles",
    month >= as.Date("2024-01-01")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = month)) +

  geom_line(
    aes(y = enrollment, color = "Actual enrollment"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = projected_enrollment,
      color = "Projected enrollment"
    ),
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = baseline_date,
    linetype = "dotted",
    color = "gray40"
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Actual enrollment" = "#2166AC",
      "Projected enrollment" = "#D97706"
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma()
  ) +

  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "3 months",
    date_labels = "%b %Y"
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Medi-Cal Enrollment in Los Angeles County",
    subtitle = "Actual enrollment compared to projected enrollment based on historical trends",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Total Medi-Cal enrollment",
    color = NULL,
    caption = "Baseline: June 2025. October 2025 data are unavailable."
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +

  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

```

# Method 2: Using predicted values from fitted regression model

Calculate enrollment predicted values using regressoin model (this is like the the method we use for our RIPA outlier analyses)

```{r}

df <- enrollment_df %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  group_modify(~ {

    # Select historical data for training the model
    pre_data <- .x %>%
      filter(
        month >= model_start,
        month <= baseline_date,
        !is.na(enrollment)
      )

    # Skip counties with insufficient historical data
    if (nrow(pre_data) < 12) {

      return(.x %>%
        mutate(
          projected_enrollment = NA_real_,
          enrollment_gap = NA_real_,
          enrollment_gap_pct = NA_real_
        ))
    }

    # Fit linear regression using historical data
    pre_model <- lm(
      enrollment ~ time,
      data = pre_data
    )

    # Predict enrollment using the fitted regression model
    .x %>%
      mutate(
        projected_enrollment = if_else(
          month >= baseline_date,
          as.numeric(predict(pre_model, newdata = .x)),
          NA_real_
        ),

        enrollment_gap =
          enrollment - projected_enrollment,

        enrollment_gap_pct =
          100 * enrollment_gap / projected_enrollment
      )

  }) %>%
  ungroup()


# Pull out diagnostics of the model for each county---------------------

library(broom)

model_diagnostics <- enrollment_df %>%
  filter(
    month >= model_start,
    month <= baseline_date,
    !is.na(enrollment)
  ) %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  filter(n() >= 12) %>%
  group_modify(~ {

    pre_model <- lm(
      enrollment ~ time,
      data = .x
    )

    glance(pre_model) %>%
      mutate(
        intercept = unname(coef(pre_model)["(Intercept)"]),
        monthly_trend = unname(coef(pre_model)["time"])
      )

  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(
    county,
    nobs,
    intercept,
    monthly_trend,
    r.squared,
    adj.r.squared,
    p.value,
    statistic,
    sigma,
    AIC,
    BIC
  )


View(model_diagnostics)

```

# Combine method 1 and method 2 into one df for one visual

```{r}

df <- enrollment_df %>%
  group_by(county) %>%
  group_modify(~ {

    # Select historical training data
    pre_data <- .x %>%
      filter(
        month >= model_start,
        month <= baseline_date,
        !is.na(enrollment)
      )

    # Extract baseline enrollment and time
    baseline <- .x %>%
      filter(month == baseline_date) %>%
      pull(enrollment)

    baseline_time <- .x %>%
      filter(month == baseline_date) %>%
      pull(time)

    # Skip counties with insufficient historical data
    if (nrow(pre_data) < 12) {

      return(.x %>%
        mutate(
          fitted_enrollment = NA_real_,
          projected_enrollment_regression = NA_real_,
          projected_enrollment_anchored = NA_real_
        ))
    }

    # Fit linear regression
    pre_model <- lm(enrollment ~ time, data = pre_data)

    # Extract historical monthly trend
    monthly_trend <- unname(coef(pre_model)["time"])

    # Check whether baseline is valid
    valid_baseline <- length(baseline) == 1 &&
      !anyNA(baseline) &&
      length(baseline_time) == 1

    .x %>%
      mutate(

        # Regression estimates during historical period
        fitted_enrollment = if_else(
          month >= model_start & month <= baseline_date,
          as.numeric(predict(pre_model, newdata = .x)),
          NA_real_
        ),

        # Method 2: Direct regression prediction
        projected_enrollment_regression = if_else(
          month >= baseline_date,
          as.numeric(predict(pre_model, newdata = .x)),
          NA_real_
        ),

        # Method 1: Baseline-anchored projection
        projected_enrollment_anchored = if (valid_baseline) {
          if_else(
            month >= baseline_date,
            baseline + monthly_trend * (time - baseline_time),
            NA_real_
          )
        } else {
          NA_real_
        }

      )

  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(

    # Enrollment gap using regression prediction
    enrollment_gap_regression =
      enrollment - projected_enrollment_regression,

    enrollment_gap_pct_regression =
      100 * enrollment_gap_regression /
      projected_enrollment_regression,

    # Enrollment gap using anchored projection
    enrollment_gap_anchored =
      enrollment - projected_enrollment_anchored,

    enrollment_gap_pct_anchored =
      100 * enrollment_gap_anchored /
      projected_enrollment_anchored

  )

# Visualize everything together

df %>%
  filter(
    county == "Los Angeles",
    month >= model_start
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = month)) +

  geom_line(
    aes(y = enrollment, color = "Actual enrollment"),
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  geom_line(
    aes(y = fitted_enrollment, color = "Historical fitted trend"),
    linewidth = 0.8,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +

  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = projected_enrollment_regression,
      color = "Regression prediction"
    ),
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +

  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = projected_enrollment_anchored,
      color = "Anchored projection"
    ),
    linewidth = 1,
    linetype = "dashed",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = baseline_date,
    linetype = "dotted"
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Actual enrollment" = "#2166AC",
      "Historical fitted trend" = "gray50",
      "Regression prediction" = "#16A34A",
      "Anchored projection" = "#D97706"
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma()
  ) +

  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "3 months",
    date_labels = "%b %Y"
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Medi-Cal Enrollment in Los Angeles County",
    subtitle = "Comparison of enrollment projection methodologies",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Total Medi-Cal enrollment",
    color = NULL,
    caption = "October 2025 actual enrollment data are unavailable."
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +

  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )


```
